turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Please complete the initial electrode inspection. Check the electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than one millimeter or mushrooming, examine the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage, and inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for any blockage.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than 1 mm or mushrooming. 2. Check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. 3. Inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Initial inspection complete. I've checked all three items and documented the findings.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect electrode cap faces for pitting deeper than 1 mm or mushrooming. 2. Check the cap shank contact surface for corrosion or mechanical damage. 3. Inspect the coolant port on each electrode arm for blockage.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the electrode caps look good. There's some minor surface wear but no severe pitting, mushrooming, or cracks visible.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode cap damage, severe pitting, mushrooming or cracking?

turns.utterance: Electrode face diameter within wear limit?

turns.utterance: Yes, the face diameter is still within the acceptable wear limit for both electrodes.

turns.utterance: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

ground_truth.node_text: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Yes, both electrodes are showing flow rates well above the minimum threshold. The cooling system is performing normally.

ground_truth.node_text: Cooling water flow rate above minimum at both electrodes?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Electrode force within plus or minus five percent of programmed schedule value?

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode force within ±5% of programmed schedule value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured force is reading about eight percent low compared to the programmed value.

ground_truth.node_text: Electrode force within ±5% of programmed schedule value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the pneumatic pressure regulator on the electrode arm to bring the force back into specification.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pneumatic pressure regulator on electrode arm

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Regulator adjusted. I've increased the pneumatic pressure to compensate for the force deficit.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust pneumatic pressure regulator on electrode arm

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Force is now reading within tolerance. The adjustment brought it back to the programmed value.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify electrode force after regulator adjustment

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Measured weld current within plus or minus three percent of scheduled value?

ground_truth.node_text: Measured weld current within ±3% of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the current is reading about four and a half percent below the scheduled value on the test weld.

ground_truth.node_text: Measured weld current within ±3% of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Access the weld controller parameter menu using the maintenance password, read the current correction factor for the affected welding schedule, and compare it against the reference value for this material stack.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following steps: 1. Access the weld controller parameter menu using the maintenance password. 2. Read the current correction factor for the affected welding schedule. 3. Compare the stored factor against the reference value for this material stack.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: I've accessed the controller and reviewed the correction factor. It appears to be set incorrectly for this material.

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following steps: 1. Access the weld controller parameter menu using the maintenance password. 2. Read the current correction factor for the affected welding schedule. 3. Compare the stored factor against the reference value for this material stack.

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Reverify weld current after controller correction.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: The current is now within specification after updating the correction factor.

ground_truth.node_text: Reverify weld current after controller correction

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Weld time within plus or minus one cycle of scheduled value?

ground_truth.node_text: Weld time within ±1 cycle of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: No, the measured weld time is running about two cycles longer than the programmed schedule.

ground_truth.node_text: Weld time within ±1 cycle of scheduled value?

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Adjust the weld timer setting in the controller schedule to bring the timing back within tolerance.

ground_truth.node_text: Adjust weld timer setting in controller schedule

turns.speaker: system
turns.utterance: Clean both electrode faces and perform a carbon transfer paper contact test. Close the electrodes at twenty-five percent of programmed force and inspect the contact pattern on each face for concentricity and coverage.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at 25% of the programmed force setting and open. Inspect the carbon transfer pattern on each face; the contact impression should be concentric and cover the full electrode face area uniformly. An off centre or crescent shaped pattern indicates electrode misalignment requiring mechanical correction.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Contact test complete. The carbon transfer pattern shows good concentric coverage on both electrode faces.

ground_truth.node_text: Clean both electrode faces and place a sheet of carbon transfer paper between them. Close the electrodes at 25% of the programmed force setting and open. turns.utterance: Electrode faces parallel, contact pattern above ninety percent of face area?

ground_truth.node_text: Complete the following steps: 1. Verify the marking controller is connected to the factory network. 2. Navigate to the archive menu and check that the last record was written successfully. 3. Confirm the archive path and file permissions are correctly configured.

turns.utterance: Immerse a calibrated thermocouple probe in the cooling water return line at the electrode holder exit. Run twenty welds at production rate and record the return line temperature at steady state.

ground_truth.node_text: Immerse a calibrated thermocouple probe in the cooling water return line at the point closest to the electrode holder exit. Allow the machine to complete 20 welds at production rate and record the return line temperature at steady state. Compare against the maximum allowable return temperature in the cooling system specification; excessive temperature indicates inadequate cooling flow or fouled heat exchanger plates.

turns.speaker: operator
turns.utterance: Temperature monitoring complete. I've recorded the steady state return temperature after the twenty-weld cycle.
